```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

The last stop covers the project plumbing: the package list, renv, git
helpers, the AI assistant files, the security audit, and tidying the R
session.

## Packages

`packages_list()` shows the packages in `settings/packages.yml` and whether
scaffold() attaches each one.

```{r}
packages_list()
```

`package_add()` records a package in settings and installs it if needed. Use
it instead of `install.packages()` so the project remembers the dependency.
broom tidies model output; open `settings/packages.yml` after this chunk to see
the new entry.

Settings writes change only the section they edit, so the rest of the file
keeps its formatting: `true`/`false` stay as written, and comments in other
files such as `settings/connections.yml` are untouched.

```{r}
package_add("broom")
tail(readLines("settings/packages.yml"), 4)
```

```{r}
bp_long <- data_read("inputs.final.bp_long")
bp_lm <- lm(systolic_change ~ treatment + age + sex, data = bp_long, subset = visit_number > 1)
broom::tidy(bp_lm, conf.int = TRUE)
```

`packages_install()` installs anything in the list that's missing. Everything
is installed here, so it has nothing to do.

```{r}
packages_install()
```

## renv

renv is off in this project. `packages_status()` still reports whether each
package in settings is installed, and says there's no lockfile to compare
with.

```{r}
renv_enabled()
```

```{r}
packages_status()
```

Turning renv on creates a project library and `renv.lock`, which takes a
while and changes the project, so these are shown but not run.
`renv_disable()` turns it off again and keeps the lockfile.

```{r}
#| eval: false
renv_enable()
packages_snapshot()
packages_status()
packages_restore()
packages_update("dplyr")
renv_disable()
```

## Git helpers

These wrap git for the repository the project sits in. Here that's the
`framework-test-projects` repo; `git_status()` says so first, and paths are
relative to this project.

```{r}
git_status(short = TRUE)
```

```{r}
git_log(n = 5)
```

`git_diff()` shows unstaged changes to tracked files. This project isn't
committed yet, so there's nothing to show.

```{r}
git_diff()
```

`git_add()`, `git_commit()`, `git_push()`, and `git_pull()` change the
repository, so they aren't run here.

```{r}
#| eval: false
git_add("notebooks/")
git_commit("Add hand-testing notebooks")
git_push()
git_pull()
```

## Pre-commit hooks

Framework can install a pre-commit hook that blocks commits of private data
or secrets. `git_hooks_list()` shows which checks are on.

```{r}
git_hooks_list()
```

Hooks belong to a repository, and this project sits inside the shared test
repo. `git_hooks_install()` refuses rather than installing hooks for the
enclosing repository; look for "inside the git repository".

```{r}
#| error: true
git_hooks_install()
```

In a project that is its own repository (`git init` at its top), these turn
the data security hook on and off.

```{r}
#| eval: false
git_hooks_enable("data_security")
git_hooks_install()
git_hooks_disable("data_security")
git_hooks_uninstall()
```

## Security audit

`git_security_audit()` checks that private folders are gitignored, that no
data or secrets are tracked now or in history, and lists data files outside
the configured folders that git would pick up. The `local-site/` bundles from
notebook 06 and `analysis.sqlite` from notebook 03 sit outside the configured
folders, but they're gitignored, so they aren't reported.

```{r}
audit <- git_security_audit()
```

The result is a list you can work with. `summary` has one row per check.

```{r}
audit$summary
```

A data file outside the configured folders that isn't ignored does show up.
This writes one to the project root (the `./` makes `data_save()` read it as a path, not a catalog name; `framework.db` records it as plain `bp_preview.csv`), audits, and removes it.

```{r}
data_save(head(bp_long), "./bp_preview.csv")
db_query("SELECT name, path FROM data WHERE name LIKE '%bp_preview%'", "framework")
audit <- git_security_audit(check_git_history = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
audit$findings$orphaned_files$path
unlink("bp_preview.csv")
```

## AI assistant context

Projects keep one `AGENTS.md` for AI assistants (`CLAUDE.md` points to it)
plus skills in `.claude/skills/`. `ai_generate_context()` returns what a fresh
`AGENTS.md` would say without writing anything.

```{r}
fresh_context <- ai_generate_context(project_name = "r-project", project_type = "project")
cat(head(strsplit(fresh_context, "\n")[[1]], 25), sep = "\n")
```

`ai_regenerate_context()` rewrites only the sections of `AGENTS.md` marked
`<!-- @framework:regenerate -->`. After `package_add("broom")` above, the
installed packages section now lists broom.

```{r}
ai_regenerate_context()
agents <- readLines("AGENTS.md")
grep("broom", agents, value = TRUE)
```

`ai_skills_update()` refreshes the Framework skills in `.claude/skills/` from
the installed package version, for after you upgrade framework. It reports
which skills it changed and which were already current.

```{r}
ai_skills_update()
```

`ai_sync_context()` is deprecated: with one `AGENTS.md` there is nothing to
sync.

```{r}
ai_sync_context()
```

## The R session

`env_summary()` describes the session: R version, attached packages, and the
largest objects in an environment.

```{r}
env_summary(envir = globalenv())
```

`env_clear()` removes objects, closes plots, and detaches packages, keeping
what you name. Framework stays attached.

```{r}
env_clear(keep = "bp_long", envir = globalenv())
ls(globalenv())
```

## Not run here

- `docs_export()` builds the documentation database for the package's GUI
  and website from `man/`. It's a tool for the package itself.
- `project_add_directory(".", "inputs_reference", "Reference", "inputs/reference")`
  adds a directory to `settings.yml` and creates it. It rewrites
  `settings.yml`, so try it by hand and look at the diff.
- `load_settings_catalog()` returns the catalog of settings the GUI edits.
- `bootstrap_project_init()` writes a legacy `init.R`.
